McClurg & Co., 1912), the eighth of the book's eleven illustrations; maker not named, undated. A wash drawing of Lee's Place on the South Branch, with a printed caption beneath it.

note: A retrospective picture, drawn about a century after the farm by a maker the book does not name, and graded tier 5 as the ladder grades every such reconstruction: it informs form and cross-checks, and is never the sole evidence for anything documented nor traced for a coordinate. What it draws, read off the image: a river in the foreground running away to the right; across it, on the far bank, a long, low single-storey house with a dark gable roof, a tall exterior stack against its left-hand gable and a lower gabled lean-to beyond that stack; along its river front three doors and six small windows in the order window, door, window, window, door, window, window, door, window; a worm (zigzag) rail fence along the bank in front of the house that turns and runs back round a large field behind it; three small gabled outbuildings in the field behind, a scatter of stumps, a dark belt of woods along the far side of the field, a canoe drawn up on the bank below the house, trees in the foreground on both sides, and two small standing figures at the house's right-hand end. It shows no haystacks.
what_it_supplies: the house's form as one illustrator imagined it in 1912: long, low, one storey, a gable roof running along the river front, an exterior stack at one gable end and a lean-to beyond it
the river front's opening set-out: three doors and six windows
the field's fence: a worm (zigzag) rail fence along the bank and round the field
the house standing close to the bank inside the fence, with the field behind it and woods beyond
what_it_does_not_supply: a maker, a date of drawing or a stated basis: nothing says the picture was drawn from a witness's description, and it may as well show the later trading house on the same premises (Hurlbut: Crafts's, 1817-1822) as the farm of 1812
any dimension, position or bearing: it is tier 5 and gives form only
colour: the plate is a monochrome halftone
haystacks: Wau-Bun puts them on the bank opposite the cabin, and the plate draws none
